title: P3 execution conventions, amendments, invariant models, move procedure and commands

sections.title: Rules every P3 item follows
sections.text:
P3 implements the recorded reference with the P3 amendments (`#amendments`, decisions D19–D23); it does not redesign it.

1. **Reference wins.** Placement, owner, marker and action are those of `knowledge/type-map` plus the rows added in `#amendments`; new signatures are those of `knowledge/contracts` plus `#scope-description`. A placement or signature that cannot be implemented as written is an amendment: stop, record `plan.py log <plan> <item> --type friction` with the evidence and ask the owner. Never ship a silent variant.
2. **No compatibility shims (D16, M16).** No `class_alias`, no forwarding classes at old FQCNs, no deprecated members, no special error text for removed things. Public 1.0 is the first public version: nothing in code, tests or docs (except `docs/upgrade.md`) speaks of 0.7.
3. **Placement is final from P3.4 on.** P3.4 adds the module PSR-4 roots; afterwards every new module file is created directly under `packages/core/modules/<module>/src` (or `stubs/`, `database/migrations/`). `src/Scopes`, `src/Audit`, `src/DevTools` and `src/Plugins/Audit` never reappear (I5). `src/Plugins/PluginContext.php` is core and stays.
4. **Publication.** A type an item creates or whose FQCN it changes carries the attribute of its marker; new types use `since: '1.0'` (from P3.13 on every attribute does, D23). After any change of a supported type run `composer api:manifest` and commit both manifests.
5. **Ownership oracle.** `tests/Arch/Fixtures/target-map.json` is the byte copy of the plan artifact `artifacts/inventory/target-map.json` with its sha256 in `target-map.sha256` (D14). A production type that is not in the oracle has no owner and fails `OwnershipScanTest`. Only an item that `#amendments` names may add rows, through the procedure in `#oracle`; never edit the JSON by hand and never add an unlisted helper class (put logic into an existing class or a private method).
6. **Allowlists are report mode** (`#allowlists`): fix → remove the entry in the same commit. A new entry is allowed only with owner P3 and only when a later P3 item of this phase removes it (name the item in the commit message). At the P3 exit every list is empty and the checks are blocking.
7. **Snapshots are regression guards (D16).** An item that changes a pinned format on purpose (manifests, `tests/Fixtures/Console/commands.json`, config defaults, doctor checks, resources, DDL fixtures) regenerates the fixture in writer mode in the same commit and lists every changed fixture in its result notes. An unexplained fixture change is a defect.
8. **Migration instruction.** Each item that changes a supported symbol, DSL, command behavior, resource or identity appends lines to `docs/upgrade.md`, section `## From 0.7 to 1.0 (instructions for AI agents)`, form `Find: <grep pattern> → Replace: <new form>`, at most one sentence of explanation. Internal FQCN moves are not listed.
9. **Tests.** Tests follow renamed code mechanically; assertions are never weakened, deleted or skipped to get green, except tests of behavior a decision removes (D19 adoption/0.7.0 replay, D20 schema-1 upgrade, D21 merge, D22 name-injected closures): those are deleted or rewritten to assert the new rule, and the item result lists them. Every new rule gets a negative test that fails without the rule.
10. **No new mechanism** beyond the reference and `#amendments`: no macros, `__call`, service locator, module bus, `class_exists` switches on module classes, plugin-id literals of another owner, or priority sorting.
11. **Runtime.** Run PHP checks with PHP 8.4 (`#commands`); system PHP 8.3 breaks SQLite snapshot reads (known core debt, not in P3 scope).

sections.title: P3 amendments to the reference (D19–D23)
sections.text:
These rows and deltas override `knowledge/type-map`, `knowledge/identities`, `knowledge/contracts`, `knowledge/target-structure` and `knowledge/architecture#persistence` where they differ.

**New type-map rows (added to the oracle by the named item, `#oracle`):**

| target FQCN | kind | owner | marker | action / phase | added by | reason |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `AzGuard\Contracts\Scopes\DescribesAssignmentScope` | interface | core | Spi(Implement) | new / P3 | P3.1 | neutral description of a definition (D21) |
| `AzGuard\Context\AssignmentScopeDescription` | class | core | Spi(Call) | new / P3 | P3.1 | value returned by `description()` (D21) |
| `AzGuard\Scopes\Internal\Query\FilterQuery` | class | scopes | internal | new / P3 | P3.2 | narrowing-only builder for module filters/adapters (D22) |
| `AzGuard\Scopes\Internal\Query\FilterGuard` | class | scopes | internal | new / P3 | P3.2 | guard of `FilterQuery` (D22) |
| `AzGuard\Sources\Internal\EvaluatesAutomaticRoles` | interface | core | internal | new / P3 | P3.3 | marker of the source that evaluates `GrantedAutomatically` roles (D5) |

Removed by decision: `Storage\Schema\StorageSchema::upgrade()` member (D20); migration `2026_10_09_000000_upgrade_azguard_storage_to_schema_2` (D20). No `ScopeLookup` class: QueryScopeDirectory keeps the lookup helpers as private methods (rule 5 instead of the D22 consequence text).

**Identities (`knowledge/identities#resources`):** `2026_10_09_000000_upgrade_azguard_storage_to_schema_2` removed (D20); `2026_10_20_000000_create_azguard_audit_log` is create-only, down() drops the table (D19); `azguard-audit-migrations` publish tag, `<date>_create_azguard_<storage>_audit_log.php` generated migration and `azguard:audit:migration {storage}` as listed. Laravel providers in `packages/core/composer.json` `extra.laravel.providers`: `AzGuard\AzGuardServiceProvider`, `AzGuard\Audit\AuditServiceProvider`, `AzGuard\DevTools\DevToolsServiceProvider`.

**Persistence (`knowledge/architecture#persistence`):** the installation-scenario table is replaced by `#persistence` below; I16 = fixed basenames, plain `publishes()`, fresh installs per driver; release-gate condition 5 reads "fresh core-only and core+Audit installs on every driver".

**Schema description:** `AssignmentScopeBindingSchema::$exactSupport` = the binding is a `QueryableAssignmentScopeDefinition` with a non-null `model()` (adapter-backed types report false, D21).

**Publication (D23):** `knowledge/contracts#rules` — every attribute carries `since: '1.0'`.

sections.title: Neutral assignment-scope description (D21): signatures and call-site map
The Scopes module guards its own extension inputs (D22)
sections.text:
- `Scopes\Internal\Query\FilterQuery` (extends `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Builder`) and `Scopes\Internal\Query\FilterGuard` reproduce exactly the narrowing-only semantics of core `PredicateBuilder`/`QueryGuard`: built from a fresh `newModelQuery()` of the definition's model, `setQuery`, `newModelInstance`, `delete`, `forceDelete` refused, shape (`PredicateBuilder::shape/validateShape`) captured before and validated after the callback, terminal execution refused through the guard. Copy the behavior, not the class names; core keeps its classes for core paths (`ResourceContextMapping`, Relation adapter).
- `EligibilityBuilder::apply/constrain` use `FilterQuery`/`FilterGuard`; `eligibleContexts()` still receives core's guarded group (D18) typed as `Builder`.
- Closure filters: invoked as `$closure($query, $runtime)`. Module `ScopeConfiguration::filters()` (compile time) rejects a closure with more than two required parameters, or whose first parameter type does not accept `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Builder`, or whose second does not accept `AzGuard\Context\AssignmentScopeRuntime` (untyped is accepted) — `DefinitionException` naming the alias. `RuntimeInvoker` is no longer used by the module.
- `Narrow::int/map` uses in module files become explicit `is_int`/`is_array` checks with the same exception type.
- `QueryScopeDirectory` (module) keeps `ModelLookup::match/label` behavior as private methods.
- Negative tests (module): a filter that calls `delete()`, replaces the query, returns a builder, adds a join/order/limit, or is a name-injected closure — each fails exactly as before (or with the new `DefinitionException` for the closure).

sections.title: Adding rows to the ownership oracle
sections.text:
Only for rows listed in `#amendments`, in the item that introduces the type:

1. Add the row to the `NEW` list in `plans/2026.10.10-№1-AZGUARD-CORE-STABILIZATION/artifacts/inventory/target_map.py` (tuple `(owner, FQCN, kind, marker, 'P3', reason)` as the existing P2 rows).
2. `cd plans/2026.10.10-№1-AZGUARD-CORE-STABILIZATION/artifacts/inventory && python3 target_map.py types-0.7.0.json target-map.json` (the input is the frozen baseline scan; never rescan).
3. `cp target-map.json ../../../../tests/Arch/Fixtures/target-map.json && sha256sum ../../../../tests/Arch/Fixtures/target-map.json | cut -d' ' -f1 > ../../../../tests/Arch/Fixtures/target-map.sha256`.
4. `git diff --stat` shows only the added rows in both JSON copies; commit them with the item.

sections.title: Mechanical type moves (P3.4, P3.8–P3.10)
sections.text:
A move changes only file location, namespace and references; no behavior. Source of truth: oracle rows (`tests/Arch/Fixtures/target-map.json`) whose `action` is `move`, `close+move` or `relocate` and whose `phase` contains `P3`, filtered to the zones/owners of the item. Procedure:

1. Generate the map with a throw-away script in the session scratchpad (not committed): `{current FQCN: target FQCN}` and `{current_path: target_path}` from those rows.
2. Write a throw-away Rector config (scratchpad) with `Rector\Renaming\Rector\Name\RenameClassRector` configured with the FQCN map and run `vendor/bin/rector process packages tests bench bin --config=<scratch>/rector-moves.php`. It rewrites `use`, docblocks, `::class`, new-expressions and same-namespace references.
3. `git mv` every file to its `target_path` (create directories), then fix its `namespace` line if Rector did not.
4. Sweep string FQCNs Rector cannot see: `git grep -nF '<old FQCN>'` (and the double-backslash JSON form) over `packages tests bench bin docs phpstan.neon rector.php phpunit.xml tests/zones.json .github` for every moved type; update config, stubs, JSON fixtures, `phpstan.neon` ignores and docs. Snapshot fixtures that pin class names (doctor checks, commands, resources, api manifests) are regenerated in writer mode, not hand-edited.
5. `__DIR__`-relative paths change depth when a file moves (`StorageMigrationCommand` → `stubs/storage-migration.stub`, `StubStore::packagePath()`, providers' `config`/`database`/`resources` paths): recompute and test each.
6. Fix allowlist entries whose `file` path moved (`tests/Arch/Allowlists/*.json`) — same entry, new path — unless the item removes them.
7. `composer dump-autoload`, `vendor/bin/pint` on changed files (beware: pint may turn docblock FQCNs into imports across zones), `composer api:manifest`.
8. Verify: `git grep -nE '<old namespace prefixes>'` returns nothing outside `plans/`, `audits/`, `docs/upgrade.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

Published types never move unless the row says so (Kernel values, events, exceptions, enums, `Storage\Schema\StorageSchema` never move, D13).

sections.title: Persistence after P3 (D19, D20): ownership, migrations, scenarios, prune model
sections.text:
**Core** — `StorageSchema::create/drop(string $storage)` build/drop exactly six tables: `permissions`, `role_grants`, `permission_grants`, `panel_state`, `subject_revisions`, `storage_state`. `upgrade()` and the second migration are deleted (D20). `packages/core/database/migrations` holds only `2026_10_01_000000_create_azguard_storage.php`, loaded with `loadMigrationsFrom` and published with plain `publishes()` under `azguard-migrations`. `azguard:storage:migration {name}` generates six tables. `StorageMigrated`, `StorageHealth`, `StorageSchema` doctor checks and `StorageHealth::HOST_KEY_COLUMNS` know no `audit_log`. Storage version mismatch: one message without the schema-1 hint.

**Audit** — `Audit\Internal\AuditSchema` creates/drops `{prefix}audit_log` for a `StorageDescriptor` with the same 14 columns, indexes, unique `event_id` and tenant pair constraint as today's `StorageSchema` audit block, built only through `Storage\Schema\IdentityColumns` (Spi(Call)) and Laravel's schema builder on the descriptor's connection. The migration `modules/audit/database/migrations/2026_10_20_000000_create_azguard_audit_log.php` creates it on `default` (down() drops it); `AuditServiceProvider` publishes the directory with plain `publishes()` under `azguard-audit-migrations` and never calls `loadMigrationsFrom`. `azguard:audit:migration {storage}` writes `database/migrations/<Y_m_d_His>_create_azguard_<storage>_audit_log.php` from `modules/audit/stubs/audit-migration.stub` (fails with exit 2 for an unknown storage and when the file exists). Doctor `audit.table` (Audit check, contributed by `AuditPlugin`): for each audited panel the writer storage has `audit_log` (error with the publish/command remedy) and its columns/indexes match `AuditSchema` (error listing differences).

**DDL fixtures (I15)** — `tests/Fixtures/Storage/ddl/<driver>.json` pins the six core tables; a second fixture per driver pins `audit_log` built by `AuditSchema`. SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB.

**Fresh-install scenarios (I16, each per driver):**

| Scenario | Expected |
|:--|:--|
| core only, package-loaded migration | six tables, doctor green, no `audit_log`, no audit migration pending |
| core only, published core migration | same; the published copy keeps the basename and runs once |
| core + Audit, default storage | `vendor:publish --tag=azguard-audit-migrations` + `migrate` → `audit_log`; audited write journals rows; doctor green; before publishing doctor `audit.table` error names the remedy |
| core + Audit, named storage | `azguard:storage:migration ledger` + `azguard:audit:migration ledger` + `migrate` → seven tables with prefix; journal rows on `ledger` |
| rollback | Audit migration down() drops `audit_log`; core down() drops six tables and leaves another owner's table untouched |

**Prune invariant model (P3.6).** *Invariant:* retention pruning deletes only `audit_log` rows of the selected panel with `occurred_at` < cutoff, never touches authority tables, revisions, epochs or events, and never blocks or is blocked by the authority write lock; concurrent journal inserts of committed operations are never lost. *Enforcement:* `Audit\Internal\JournalPruner` selects up to 1000 ids (`panel = ? AND occurred_at < ?` ordered by id) and deletes `WHERE id IN (…)` in one short transaction on the storage connection per batch, repeating until a batch is empty; a deadlock/serialization failure (SQLSTATE 40001/40P01, MySQL 1213) retries only that batch up to 3 times, then the command fails with exit 1. No `panel_state` lock, no `StorageMutation`, no `ChangePipeline`. *Bypass closed:* `ChangePipeline::pruneJournal` is deleted; core contains no `audit_log` literal (I2). *Interfering pairs:*

| Pair | Expected |
|:--|:--|
| prune ↔ concurrent grant (participant insert of new rows) | new rows (occurred_at ≥ cutoff) survive; grant commits; no deadlock surfaces to the writer (writer retries are the core's own) |
| prune ↔ prune (two processes, same panel) | rows deleted once; both exit 0; count sum equals deleted rows |
| prune ↔ host transaction holding the authority lock | prune does not wait for `panel_state` |
| prune with `--before` | never deletes rows newer than the retention cut-off |

Checked by engine tests (`tests/Engines`, group `engines`) on pgsql, mysql and mariadb.

sections.title: Allowlists and blocking switch
sections.text:
| File | P3 duty |
|:--|:--|
| `tests/Arch/Allowlists/i2.json` | `BatchInputs`, `SchemaBuilder` → P3.1; `ChangePipeline`/`StorageHealth`/`StorageSchema` `audit_log` → P3.5/P3.6; `AzGuardServiceProvider` command imports → P3.6 (AuditPruneCommand) and P3.7 (DevTools). Empty after P3.7. |
| `tests/Arch/Allowlists/i3.json` | stays empty |
| `tests/Arch/Allowlists/i4.json` | `EligibilityBuilder`, `QueryScopeDirectory` → P3.2; `AuditPruneCommand` → P3.6; `InstallCommand`, `MakeCommand`, `Layout`, `models-migration.stub` → P3.7. Empty after P3.7. |
| `tests/Arch/Allowlists/i5.json` | `src/Scopes`, `src/Audit`, `src/Plugins/Audit` → P3.4. Empty after P3.4. |
| `tests/Fixtures/InactiveCost/allowlist.json` | `audit_log` module-table-required → P3.5. Empty after P3.5. |
| `tests/Fixtures/Parity/i7-allowlist.json` | stays empty |

P3.12 turns I2, I3, I4, I5 and I13 blocking: `tests/Arch/invariants.json` `blocking: "now"` for them, the report-mode tests assert an empty list and fail on any violation, and the allowlist files are deleted (with their readers) or reduced to `[]` with a test that they stay empty.

sections.title: Activation matrix (P3.12)
sections.text:
Fixture panels under `tests/Fixtures/Activation/` exercised by `tests/Feature/Activation/ActivationMatrixTest.php` on SQLite (group `database` for the driver lanes):

| Configuration | Assertions |
|:--|:--|
| core only | boot, check, grant, revoke, visibility, doctor: zero module services resolved (container resolution log), zero queries on module tables (query log), no `audit_log`, `scopeDeclaration()` null → mode None |
| + Scopes on A, B without | A interprets mode/aliases; B denies non-global requests (`assignment_scope_not_accepted`) and stored scoped rows of B are inert |
| + Audit on A, B without, one storage | A writes journal rows (same `event_id` as dispatched event); B writes none |
| two panels, different options | different modes/retention; fingerprints differ; options objects not shared |
| module removed after use | rows retained; scopes inert and fail closed; journaling stops; revoke/expiry/prune still work |
| DevTools outside console | no `azguard:make:*`/`azguard:install`/`azguard:stubs` registered; `scaffold` section still validated only when DevTools registered it |

**Core without module roots (I13, I19):** `bin/consumer-fixture.sh` gains a `core-only` mode that builds the core archive with `modules/` removed and `extra.laravel.providers` reduced to `AzGuard\AzGuardServiceProvider` (and PSR-4 reduced to `AzGuard\`), installs it in a clean Laravel app, runs migrate, `azguard:doctor`, one grant and one check. It is blocking in the consumer job.

sections.title: Validation commands and environment
sections.text:
Run from the repository root with PHP 8.4: `mkdir -p <scratch>/php84 && ln -sf /usr/bin/php8.4 <scratch>/php84/php` and prefix commands with `PATH=<scratch>/php84:$PATH` (composer is `/usr/local/bin/composer`). Database services (Docker context `default`): on this machine PostgreSQL 25432, MySQL 23306, MariaDB 23307 (check `docker ps`); export `PGSQL_PORT=25432 MYSQL_PORT=23306 MARIADB_PORT=23307` before driver commands.

| Purpose | Command |
|:--|:--|
| Architecture checks | `php -d memory_limit=1G vendor/bin/pest tests/Arch --fail-on-skipped` |
| Parity, I7, inactive cost, format snapshots | `php -d memory_limit=1G vendor/bin/pest tests/Feature/Parity tests/Feature/InactiveCost tests/Regression --fail-on-skipped` |
| Full SQLite suite | `composer test` |
| Database lanes | `composer test:db -- pgsql --parallel`, `composer test:db -- mysql --parallel`, `composer test:db -- mariadb --parallel` |
| Engine suites | `composer test:db -- pgsql --engines`, `composer test:db -- mysql --engines`, `composer test:db -- mariadb --engines` |
| Static analysis, style, refactor, manifests | `composer analyse && composer lint:check && composer refactor:check && composer api:check` |
| Type coverage | `composer test:types` |
| Consumer archives | `bash bin/consumer-fixture.sh` (see its usage; P3.12 adds `core-only`) |

**Composer autoload after editing `packages/core/composer.json`:** the root installs the package through a path repository, so the new PSR-4 roots and providers reach `vendor/composer` only after `composer update axiomasoft/azguard axiomasoft/azguard-filament --no-interaction` (then `composer dump-autoload`). If the agent is not permitted to run `composer update`, stop and ask the owner to run it (`! composer update axiomasoft/azguard axiomasoft/azguard-filament`). `composer.lock` is gitignored.

Per item, long runs (full suite, database lanes, engines, type coverage) are `impact` checks; they are acceptance only in the phase exit item P3.14. Diagnostics (single-test reruns) are never acceptance evidence.
